summary: Spike of 429 throttles perceived as timeouts; client retries amplify latency and request queueing
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden increase in perceived request timeouts starting 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC. Symptoms include long end-to-end response times (>10s), many client-side retries, and an accompanying spike in 429 responses from the API. Impact: Production traffic for GreenSea Health's clinical summarization flow was disrupted for ~45 minutes, causing delayed responses to end users and degrading downstream pipelines that depend on timely embeddings. Hypothesis: A short-lived tightening of rate-limiter windows combined with aggressive client retry behavior caused request pileup. Clients interpreted intermittent 429s as 'server not responding' and retried immediately without honoring Retry-After headers, amplifying load and feeding the serving runtime's queue, resulting in higher tail latency and additional 5xx/timeout symptoms.
steps_to_reproduce: From a customer environment under production traffic profile, send mixed generation and embedding requests with sustained RPS near their committed rate
Simulate a transient rate-limit policy change (reduce per-client token bucket from 2000 TPS to 400 TPS for 60s) at the api-gateway
Have client SDK configured with immediate retries (no exponential backoff) and retry on 429 as if it were a network timeout
Observe server logs for 429 spikes, increased queue lengths on the serving runtime, and higher P95/P99 latencies
logs: 2026-03-10T09:16:03Z api-gateway INFO client_id=gs-health-02 status=429 X-RateLimit-Limit=400 X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 Retry-After=2
2026-03-10T09:16:04Z client-sdk WARN request_id=abc123 response_status=429 reason=rate_limited attempt=1 will_retry=true
investigation_notes: Confirmed transient policy adjustment: rate-limiter rule 'burst-control-v2' was redeployed at 09:15 with a lower default bucket for the customer segment due to a separate autoscale sensitivity change (PR #1983).
Rate-limit headers were present and correctly set (Retry-After=2s) in 429 responses; customer SDK was not honoring Retry-After and retried with 0s backoff leading to retry storm.
Serving runtime metrics show queue growth coincident with 429 spike; CPU and GPU utilization remained within acceptable bounds, indicating queueing rather than resource exhaustion.
Observed a secondary effect where retries increased token consumption for the customer's quota, pushing them closer to quota thresholds and causing additional 429s from quota enforcement.
No evidence of a widespread platform outage; impact contained to customer namespace due to their retry behavior and the transient rate-limit change.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:02 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports timeouts and long delays. Collected request IDs and sample logs. Asking SRE to validate rate-limiter changes around 09:15 UTC.
2026-03-10 10:18 - Luca Romero (SRE): Confirmed deployment of 'burst-control-v2' at 09:15. Rolling back that redeploy to previous config removed the tightened buckets; observing reduced 429s.

2026-03-10 10:35 - Elsa Park (Customer Success): Notified GreenSea Health of rollback and suggested they instrument SDK retry handling. Customer says their SDK had custom retry logic that ignores Retry-After.
2026-03-11 08:45 - Luca Romero (SRE): Added temporary per-client queue limit and increased per-minute quota for GreenSea Health to prevent immediate throttling while we coordinate SDK fixes.
2026-03-12 14:05 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirmed recovery and reduced retry rate after SDK patch. Request to document SDK best-practices and add proactive alerts for retry storms.
resolution_notes: Rolled back 'burst-control-v2' change to restore previous per-client token bucket sizes at 09:22 UTC (mitigation).
Applied a temporary per-customer soft-quota increase and a short-term queue cap to limit retry amplification while the customer deployed SDK fixes.
Customer deployed SDK patch to honor Retry-After and implement exponential backoff with full jitter (recommended: initial_delay=200ms, multiplier=2, max_delay=10s).
Created KB: 'Handling 429s and avoiding retry storms' and added links to SDK examples. Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/429+Best+Practices

Action items: (1) Add retry-storm alerting to api-gateway (P2) assigned to Luca; (2) Add a postmortem entry and update autoscale runbook to avoid inadvertent burst tightening (P1) assigned to Platform team.
